title: Father's lodge drill corps and first brass bands
summary: His father drills boys in the Tabernacle Lodge drill corps, teaching rhythm, and they travel to Arkansas towns where he hangs around brass bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: My father in the meantime was a drill master. He belonged to a lodge called "The Tabernacle Lodge," and they featured at their yearly convention different troops of boys and women drilling, and the best team would always win a prize. So, my father put me in the drill corps, and the type of drilling was in rhythm. It was your left foot was always the odd number, and your right foot was always the even number. Like one, two, left, right, left, right. Left one, right two.

And all the kids that drilled with him had to have that rhythm or that sense of rhythm in order to belong to the drill corps. And in drilling we would make different letters like the letter A, the letter B, the letter C, and we would do it in uniform. And every summer we would go from -- to various cities in the state of Arkansas.

And I can remember the first city that we visited was Forest City, Arkansas. And I remember there were no paved streets. All the streets were dusty and dirt. And they had a brass band there playing. And the brass band was playing a song named "Dar-dane-lla." And I thought that was the prettiest band, the prettiest song -- one of the prettiest songs I'd ever heard. And I just hung around that band every day that the band played. Of course, it was about for three days we were there.
And each year we would do to various cities, like Hot Springs one year, Pine Bluff another year, sometimes back to Little Rock one year, then back to Hot Springs, and on and on.
